newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX fuel oil futures trade first time since 1995.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX fuel oil futures trade first time since 1995.

text.p: The fuel oil futures contract listed on the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) traded for the first time on Monday since August 1995.
The contract has been dormant since August 1995 when traders withdrew from the market owing to a lack of liquidity.
But SIMEX did not delist the contract and lately has held discussions with traders about ways to make the derivative more attractive.
The second position December contract traded 10 lots at $119.50 per tonne, brokers said.
Market sources said at least two international brokerages have been brokering the contract on Monday.
The fuel oil contract was launched in February 1989 but trade ground to a halt because traders said the specifications were out of line with the physical market.

These included physical delivery being against 4.0 percent sulphur content fuel oil and a wide delivery window between the fifth working day and 20th working day each month. Sellers had the call on the date range and port for delivering the fuel oil.
Market sources said SIMEX was now considering reducing the sulphur content to a maximum of 3.5 percent.
The delivery window would be narrowed to between 11th and 20th day of the month with sellers having the call on the delivery port and buyers the call on the delivery dates.
The proposed changes are yet to be approved by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS).
The trade on Monday was against the existing specifications.
Market sources said there was no specific reason why trading had resumed.

However, SIMEX President Ang Swee Tian told Reuter by telephone on Friday "the trading community has expressed keen interest on the contract and a group of them are trying to make a concerted effort to try to revive and re-activate the contract."
